name: La Monte Young
hook: A composer of very long, very loud held notes, whose early-1960s group put John Cale on the path to the Velvet Underground.
blurb: La Monte Young was born in Bern, Idaho, in 1935. From the late 1950s he wrote music made of notes held for a very long time, sometimes for hours. His 'Trio for Strings' (1958), built from long held tones and long silences, is usually named as a founding work of minimalism. From 1962 in New York he led a group, later called the Theatre of Eternal Music, that played loud, amplified drones in just intonation, a tuning based on pure ratios, with Marian Zazeela, Tony Conrad, John Cale and, from 1965, Terry Riley. Cale played viola in it, and brought that sound with him when he started the Velvet Underground. Almost none of its recordings have been released: Young has said he is the only composer, Conrad argued the work was made together, and the dispute has kept the tapes in the archive. Few of Young's recordings are in print at all, so he is an influence more read about than heard. Brian Eno called Young's 'X for Henry Flynt' a cornerstone of his own work (1981).
